verdict.rationale: Bitwarden describes itself as an open source password manager in its llms.txt, and a first-party repository (bitwarden/mcp-server) is published under GPL-3.0. Community reports also confirm Bitwarden relicensed back to a Free/Open License after the SDK relicensing controversy. However, no first-party evidence names the source repositories or licenses for the core clients and server. missing for 10: first-party documentation linking the core client and server source repositories with their specific open licenses, clarity on whether the SDK and all components are fully open-licensed after the relicensing controversy, and hands-on verification of browsing the main product source.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license

citations.quote: The most trusted open source password manager for passwords, passkeys, and secrets
First-party repo (bitwarden/mcp-server, GPL-3.0), published to npm.
Thank you to Bitwarden for relicensing back to Free/Open License
